title: Draft schema for x-bte annotation refactor
description: Manually-written schema for x-bte annotation refactor. Work-in-progress.

info.description: Required, fixed field in OpenAPI schema. Provides metadata about the API.

x-bte-operations.description: [Add definition of operation here.] Keys are user-defined names (allowed characters set using patternProperties).

^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$.description: This section defines a single operation. Properties are snake_case.

support_batch.description: Can multiple input IDs be sent in 1 request (true) or not (false)

response_field_root.$comment: see 12/19 notes! Using this for Biothings is complicated - depends on pagination or not.

inputs.description: Describes the input IDs that the API accepts.

use_all_namespaces.description: Only use when the namespaces array has >1 element. If an input entity has synonymous IDs from >1 namespace listed in the 'namespaces' section, should the tool generate queries using all of those IDs (true)? True implies that the API may have different data for the same thing but under different ID namespaces, and you want to retrieve all of that data. Or should the tool only use the IDs for 1 namespace - the first in the 'namespaces' section that it has IDs for (false)? False implies that the API has already done an 'entity-resolution' step and an ID from any namespace would retrieve the same data. If this field isn't specified, the tool defaults to 'false' behavior.
use_all_namespaces.$comment: While `outputs` also has this field, the description is different.

items.$comment: maybe add id_field and capture regex? Confused...See 12/20 notes

prefix.$comment: reused in outputs, turn into $ref to $def. Remember, should be biolink-model format. If not specified in biolink-model, use bioregistry format.

name_field.$comment: reused in outputs, turn into $ref to $def

replace_prefix.$comment: reused in outputs, turn into $ref to $def. Prefix that the API actually uses when it differs from the biolink-model/CURIE format (':' delimiter). must include both the prefix and the delimiter

id_field.$comment: see 12/20 notes. for batch-queries. Field in response that contains input ID that matches the response hit

outputs.description: output ID info in API response

use_all_namespaces.description: Only use when the namespaces array has >1 element. If 1 hit in the response has output IDs from >1 namespace listed in the 'namespaces' section, should the tool ingest all those IDs (true)? True implies that the API may return multiple entities/answers in 1 hit. Or should the tool only ingest the ID(s) from 1 namespace - the first in the 'namespaces' section that it finds IDs for (false)? False implies that either (1) 1 hit only has 1 output ID, or (2) the multiple output IDs in 1 hit represent the same entity so only 1 of the IDs is needed. If this field isn't specified, the tool defaults to 'false' behavior. We think setting this field to true will be rare (edge case).

namespaces.description: not same as inputs.namespace! diff required fields

capture_regex.$comment: see 12/20 notes. Not sure if this is just for outputs or not.

exclude_namespace_combos.description: This field is used only when inputs.namespaces and outputs.namespaces both have >1 element. If the certain input/output namespaces combos don't exist in the API's data, these combos can be listed here. When this field is not present, the tool will assume that all combos of input and output namespace are theoretically possible.

items.description: 2-element array: the first element is the input namespace's prefix, the second is output namespace's prefix.

items.$comment: $ref to prefix. Since these will be prefixes.

request_info.description: all info needed to generate query to API goes here
request_info.$comment: complex logic: 'at least 1 of several fields` should exist, but if some of those fields exist, then others shouldn't

path.$comment: same as in paths part of openapi spec

content_type.$comment: Value is http standard content type. Default (not specified) is application/json. User is then responsible for making request_body's contents match this type

use_pagination.description: Is this operation using API pagination (true), or not (false)?
use_pagination.$comment: For now, note info needed for/related to pagination in notes doc. Deciding where this info goes and its format later.

pagination.$comment: placeholder reminder. Won't know format until implementation? See 12/19 notes

predicate.description: This is the biomedical-science semantic type of the relationship between the input and output entities. The value must be a predicate in the biolink-model: it should be the most specific predicate that matches the relationship. Predicates labeled 'mixin' should be used carefully (read yaml spec before using). The format is snake_case, no prefix. Validation is currently just on format, so it doesn't check whether the value actually exists in the biolink-model version our tool is using.
predicate.$comment: For full validation, this would need enum of biolink-model predicates. And would need to be maintained, up-to-date with biolink-model version our tool is using.

provenance.$comment: complex!!! one of 3 schemas (two object, 1 array). Have some nested parts that are kinda repetitive, can make $ref to $def.

if.$comment: If document has one of {x-bte tag, info.x-bte-info, components.x-bte-operations}, then the others should also be present. See original and other schemas for examples of how to write this. Don't need to write out the tags section elsewhere in schema.

category.description: This is the biomedical-science semantic type of the entities represented by these IDs. The value must be a class (aka node category) in the biolink-model: it should be the most specific class that fits most of the entities. Avoid using classes labeled 'mixin' when possible. The format is PascalCase, no prefix. Validation is currently just on format, so it doesn't check whether the value actually exists in the biolink-model version our tool is using.
category.$comment: For full validation, this would need enum of acceptaable biolink-model node categories (not mixins and must be bioentities?). And would need to be maintained, up-to-date with biolink-model version our tool is using.
